newsitem.title: UK: Brady market focuses on Brazil after reform vote.
newsitem.headline: Brady market focuses on Brazil after reform vote.

text.p: Brazil stole the limelight in the emerging countries debt market on Thursday with demand boosted by news that the Brazilian government defeated an opposition motion.
Opposition parties attempted unsuccessfully to sink the government's civil service bill, which allows the administration to fire workers deemed incompetent.
The bill also breaks the lifetime job guarantees of civil servants that were enshrined in the constitution but put an increasing strain on the country's public finances.

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso has insisted that civil service reform, along with a shakeup of Brazil's endebted pension system, are crucial to the long-term prospects of the country's new-found economic stability.
At 1100 GMT, Brazil "C" bonds were bid at 83.50.
Dealers said there was resistance at 84.0 where profit-taking prevented the price from heading higher.

They said there was also strong demand for Brazil's 30-year bond. The $3.0 billion 30-year global bonds were priced to yield 395 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes and were last trading at 357 b.p. over, dealers said.
"Clients are buying the Brazil 2027 and the 'C' bonds," a dealer said.
New issues dealers also said there was some selling pressure on Russia as investors who were "overweight" the bonds took profit.
"There is some selling pressure on Minfins tranches 3, 4, 5 and 6," a dealer said.
"The market is weighed down in Russia and at some stage they've got to start taking profit," a dealer said.

Some attention was also on the U.S. producer price data due on Friday and consumer price figures out on Wednesday. A Reuters poll forecast June PPI to remain unchanged from May levels at minus 0.3 pct. -- Hayley Pienaar, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7718
